body:
Actually it is related. This works in 2.2.4 but not in 2.3.0.

I will test this again with the fix for #13327

This still reproduces with 2.3.1.

I will fix this but there are work-arounds below that will allow you to work in 2.3.0 and 2.3.1.

**What went wrong**
The reason we fail is because we changed to no longer user TypeScript to resolve the location of symbols but, rather, rely on the content of .metadata.json files which now encode enough information for us to resolve symbols.

If we run into a version 1 metadata file we will auto upgrade the metadata, copying the necessary information from the .d.ts files next to it into the metadata before we continue processing.

However, we neglected to auto-upgrade missing files. That is, if a .d.ts files has no .metadata.json file (which was valid for version 1 but is not longer valid for version 3) then we should "auto-upgrade" an empty metadata file instead of using an empty metadata file.

**Work around**
You have a couple of work-arounds for this.
1. RECOMMEND: change your main.d.ts to main.ts (replacing ./lib with ./src) and have `ngc` build the .metadata.json file  and the main.js file. This requires modifying the "main" and "typings" in your package to point to the generated files in "lib".

2. Include the .metadata.json file along side the main.d.ts that `ngc` would have produced.  Which is:
``` [{"__symbolic":"module","version":3,"metadata":{},"exports":[{"from":"./lib/cell.component"},{"from":"./lib/grid.component"},{"from":"./lib/grid.module"}]},{"__symbolic":"module","version":1,"metadata":{}}]```

I highly recommend doing (1) above because the metadata file will change and we plan to require .metadata.json files beginning with version 4.0.0. If you make the recommended changes you will be compatible with 4.0.0 without modification. If you use (2) you will need to update the metadata yourself if we start requiring a new version.

I have made the recommended modifications locally and can send you a PR to your repository with the changes if you like.

Hi @chuckjaz thanks very much, that's great. I'd appreciate a PR if you have it all ready to go, that would definitely help.

Thanks again for looking at this - we really appreciate it.
thanks very much @chuckjaz - should I close this issue now?
No. I am using this issue to track the underlying problem so other libraries will not need to work around this.

All .d.ts files without metadata in v1 were considered to not have metadata for v3 so re-export information was lost and symbols reexported by these modules could not be resolved.

A .d.ts file with no metadata will get metadata from the .d.ts file which will include the re-exports in that file.

issue.title: Directory appended to outDir if 3rd party dependencies include .ts files

repository.name: TypeScript
repository.description: TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that compiles to clean JavaScript output.

issue.body:
<!-- BUGS: Please use this template. -->
<!-- QUESTIONS: This is not a general support forum! Ask Qs at http://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/typescript -->
<!-- SUGGESTIONS: See https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript-wiki/blob/master/Writing-Good-Design-Proposals.md -->

**TypeScript Version:**  2.1.1 / nightly (2.2.0-dev.201xxxxx)

**Code**
This is a compiler issue, I have created a git repo that quickly reproduces the issue - https://github.com/dmarginian/ag-grid-ng2-ts-issue.git.  Please follow the README to reproduce the problem.

**Expected behavior:**
Consistent outDir behavior which is not impacted by 3rd party distributions.  No compilation of 3rd party ts when a d.ts is present.  This is consistent with the FAQ: 

"To do so, the compiler needs the definition of a module, this could be a .ts file for your own code, or a .d.ts for an imported definition files."

This implies ts files are used for my code and .d.ts files are used for imported 3rd parties.   

Related issues: https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/issues/6964

**Actual behavior:**
When 3rd party dependencies include .ts files in their distribution the source directory is appended to outDir and all compiled js is under the source directory (e.g. outDir/src).  If the .ts files are manually removed from the 3rd party the source directory is not appended to outDir. Please see https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/13307#issuecomment-267487799 for the reasons why ag-grid-ng2 is including .ts files in their distribution.

If the rootDir flag is used an error occurs which indicates tsc is attempting to compile the 3rd party:
error TS6059: File '/home/david/dev/projects/ms-ng2-common-modules/ts-issue/node_modules/ag-grid-ng2/main.ts' is not under 'rootDir' '/home/david/dev/projects/ms-ng2-common-modules/ts-issue/src'. 'rootDir' is expected to contain all source files.
